hints: Notice the wire gives diameter $1.22 \text{ mm}$, so halve it to get radius $0.61 \text{ mm}$ and convert to $0.61 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$ before finding cross-sectional area.
Recall Young modulus links the $37 \text{ N}$ force and $3.6 \text{ m}$ length to stress and strain as $E = (F/A)/(x/L)$.
Rearrange to $x = FL/(AE)$ with $A = \pi r^2$, then substitute $F$, $L$, $r$ and $E = 1.17 \times 10^{11} \text{ Pa}$ and convert the result to $\text{mm}$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: $L = 3.6 \text{ m}$, $F = 37 \text{ N}$, $E = 1.17 \times 10^{11} \text{ Pa}$, and diameter $= 1.22 \text{ mm}$ so radius $r = 0.61 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}$.
Calculate the cross-sectional area: $A = \pi r^2 = \pi \times (0.61 \times 10^{-3})^2 \approx 1.17 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}^2$.
State the Young modulus relation for a wire obeying Hooke's law: $E = \frac{F/A}{x/L}$.
Evaluate the numerator $37 \times 3.6 = 133.2$ and denominator $\approx 1.37 \times 10^5$, giving $x \approx 9.7 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m} \approx 0.97 \text{ mm}$.
